newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesians attack churches, Chinese temple.
newsitem.headline: Indonesians attack churches, Chinese temple.

text.p: A mob of Indonesian Moslems damaged churches and a Chinese temple on Thursday following reports that a Christian had insulted them, witnesses said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties during the rampage at Rengasdengklok, about 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta.
Witnesses said five churches were damaged but police gave the number as four and also said two arrests were made.

"Hundreds of people shouting Allahu Akbar (God is Greatest) attacked five churches and one Chinese temple this morning with stones. They smashed the windows, music instruments and also the Bible," one witness told Reuters by telephone.

The man, a church attendant whose church was among those attacked, said the rampage was apparently sparked by a report that a Christian trader had complained that Moslems performing their evening prayer were too noisy.
"The trader's house and shop have been destroyed by the mob. They also killed the pets kept by our church," the attendant said.
A policeman reached by phone in Rengasdengklok on Thursday said four churches had been attacked in the latest incident.
"Four churches have been attacked by the mob. We have arrested two people. The situation has returned to normal," he said. The policeman declined to give other details.
Last month, four people died after an angry mob went on the rampage in Tasikmalaya in Western Java, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches.
The violence was sparked by reports of police brutality towards a Moslem religious teacher.
Residents said many shops in the town were closed.
